[NCBK.2.11] **The halt latch can be read.** `ds_engine_halted(e, &halted,
&fault)` reports whether the engine has halted ([NCBK.2.9]) and, if it has,
the cause: the `ds_engine_fault_t` the `DS_EV_ENGINE_ERROR` event carried
([NCBK.2.10]). On an engine that has not halted, `halted` is false and `fault`
is `DS_ENGINE_FAULT_UNSPECIFIED`. On an engine a failed load spent
([RDSC.9.8]), `halted` is true and `fault` is `DS_ENGINE_FAULT_UNSPECIFIED`: no
`EngineError` was raised, and the load's own status was the cause.

It reads the latch and nothing else, so it is one of the calls that remain
valid after the halt ([NCBK.2.9]). An integrator
that dropped the event, or learned of the halt only from a
`DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED` status, can still learn the cause.
